questions.stem: What does specific heat capacity measure?

options.text: The temperature at which a substance melts
The energy needed to raise the temperature of 1 kg of a substance by 1 degrees C
The rate of heat transfer through a substance
The total energy stored in a substance

questions.explanation: Specific heat capacity (c) is the amount of energy required to raise the temperature of 1 kg of a substance by 1 degrees C (or 1 K).

questions.stem: What is the equation linking energy, mass, specific heat capacity, and temperature change?
questions.explanation: The equation is E = mc(delta T), where E is energy in joules, m is mass in kg, c is specific heat capacity in J/(kg degrees C), and delta T is the temperature change.

questions.stem: How much energy is needed to heat 2 kg of water from 20 degrees C to 80 degrees C? (c = 4200 J/(kg degrees C))
Water has a specific heat capacity of 4200 J/(kg degrees C). This means compared to most other substances, water:

options.text: Requires a lot of energy to change temperature

questions.explanation: Water has a very high specific heat capacity, meaning it requires a large amount of energy to change its temperature. This is why it is used in heating systems and why coastal areas have milder climates.

questions.stem: A metal spoon heats up faster than water in hot soup because metal has:

options.text: A higher boiling point than water
A higher specific heat capacity than water
A lower specific heat capacity than water
The same specific heat capacity as water

questions.explanation: Metals have a much lower specific heat capacity than water. Less energy is needed per kg per degree, so the metal heats up faster for the same energy input.

questions.stem: A 500 g aluminium block absorbs 13,500 J of energy. By how much does its temperature rise? (c = 900 J/(kg degrees C))
questions.explanation: delta T = E / (mc) = 13,500 / (0.5 x 900) = 13,500 / 450 = 30 degrees C. Note: convert 500 g to 0.5 kg.

questions.stem: What is the unit of specific heat capacity?
questions.explanation: Specific heat capacity is measured in J/(kg degrees C) or equivalently J/(kg K), representing joules per kilogram per degree of temperature change.
